operator.payload: When `--format` is used with selected fields, should the command reject the table-only `--field`/`--field-id` options, or should it continue emitting the existing structured output and ignore them?
operator.answer: OPERATOR_ANSWER: Reject the command clearly. `--field` and `--field-id` conflict with explicit formatted or JSON output; they must not be ignored.

operator.payload: If the same underlying field is selected more than once (for example, once by `--field Status` and once by `--field-id <Status-ID>`), should the table show duplicate columns in the order requested, or reject the duplicate selection?
operator.answer: OPERATOR_ANSWER: `--field` and `--field-id` cannot be combined, so the stated mixed-form example must be rejected. No additional product constraint applies to duplicate selections within a single permitted flag form; preserve the requested columns in order.

operator.payload:
Add repeatable `--field <name>` and `--field-id <id>` options to `gh project item-list`.

Behavior:
- The two selection options are mutually exclusive. Supplying both produces a clear flag-validation error.
- Either selection option conflicts with explicit output formatting (`--format`, including JSON and its jq/template variants). The command fails clearly instead of ignoring the selection or changing structured output.
- With no selection, output and request behavior remain unchanged.
- With selections, resolve every requested entry against the project fields already returned by the existing item-list query. No separate field-ID or field-list preflight request is made.
- `--field` matches project field names case-insensitively. A missing name fails with the requested name and available field names; an ambiguous case-insensitive match fails with the matching IDs and directs the user to `--field-id`.
- `--field-id` matches exactly. An unknown ID fails with available `name (id)` candidates.
- Repeated entries within one allowed option are retained, in the exact requested order, including repeated selections.
- The base columns remain `Type`, `Title`, `Number`, `Repository`, and `ID`; selected field columns are appended in requested order and use the resolved project field’s canonical name as the header.
- Each row shows the selected item field value, or an empty cell when that item has no value for the selected field. Rendering is human-readable: text/date/single-select values directly; number without avoidable formatting noise; iteration and milestone by title; labels, users, reviewers, pull requests as comma-separated labels/logins/URLs; and repository by URL.
- Resolution happens before table rendering, so invalid/ambiguous selection never produces a partial or misleading table. Existing structured export output is unchanged.

Tests will cover option parsing and conflicts, case-insensitive name resolution, unknown/ambiguous names and unknown IDs, requested column order/repetition, representative field-value renderings and blanks, formatted-output rejection, and no extra preflight request.
operator.answer:
DESIGN_CHANGES_REQUIRED

- Normalize selected-cell text by removing carriage returns and replacing newlines with spaces, including multiline values in all supported field types.

findings.title: Rendering tests omit several supported value variants
findings.evidence: pkg/cmd/project/item-list/item_list_fields_test.go:401-485 tests date, iteration, labels, number, single-select, milestone, an unknown variant, and text normalization, but not text rendering itself, users, reviewers, pull requests, or repository values.
findings.why: Those variants are required output behavior, so regressions in their formatting would not be caught by the added focused tests.
findings.suggestedFix: Add table-value tests for text, users, reviewers, pull requests, and repository values, including at least one multiline value outside the text variant.

reviewerResult.summary: Implementation aligns with the approved behavior and focused tests pass. No critical or major defects found.
